greetSimpler.en: Today we sort angles into kinds by their size.

asidePark.en: Once we finish naming these angles, we will surely talk about {aside}.

asidePark.hi: {aside} ki baat bhi hogi, bas yeh kon pehchaanna khatam ho jaaye.
asidePark.en: We'll talk about {aside} too, right after naming these angles.

asidePark.hi: Haan, {aside} wali baat pakki, thodi der mein usi par lautenge.
asidePark.en: Yes, the {aside} bit is a promise, and we'll come back to it soon.

hook.convey: angles get names by how far they open, measured against a square corner (90°): a bat lifted a little, straight up, or swung far back; the corner of a drawing sheet as the 90° yardstick

use.hi: Batting ke waqt bat zameen se thoda utha toh bat aur zameen ke beech chhota angle banta hai. Bat bilkul seedha khada ho toh woh kona page ke kone jaisa hota hai, aur peeche tak jaaye toh usse bhi bada angle.
use.en: While batting, if the bat lifts a little off the ground, a small angle forms between bat and ground. If the bat stands straight up, that corner is like the corner of a page, and if it swings far back the angle is bigger still.

use.hi: Drawing sheet ka har kona ek right angle hai, 90°. Isi kone se hum doosre angles ko naapte hain: kone se patla angle ek type ka, kone se zyada khula doosre type ka.
use.en: Every corner of a drawing sheet is a right angle, 90°. We size other angles against this corner: an angle thinner than the corner is one type, one opened wider than the corner is another.

explain.convey: right angle (samkon) = exactly 90°, the square corner of a page; any angle less than 90° (and more than 0°) = acute (nyun kon); board: a 90° and a 40° angle side by side; the child names the 40° one from the rule

point.hi: Board par do angles hain. Pehla 90° ka hai, yeh right angle hai, samkon, bilkul page ke kone jaisa. Jo angle 90° se kam khula ho, use acute angle, yaani nyun kon, kehte hain. Doosra angle 40° ka hai.
point.en: There are two angles on the board. The first is 90°; it is a right angle, exactly like the corner of a page. An angle that opens less than 90° is called an acute angle. The second angle is 40°.

prompt.hi: Yeh 40° wala angle kis type ka hai: acute ya right angle?
prompt.en: What type is the 40° angle on the board: acute or right angle?

why.hi: 40° right angle ke 90° se kam khula hai
why.en: 40° opens less than the 90° of a right angle

simpler.hi: Page ka kona 90° ka hota hai, woh right angle hai. Ab 40° ko 90° se milao, aur dekho woh kone se kam khula hai ya zyada.
simpler.en: A page corner is 90°, a right angle. Now compare 40° with 90° and see if it opens less or more than the corner.

explain.convey: obtuse (adhik kon) = more than 90° and less than 180°: opened past the square corner but not yet flat; board: a 90° and a 130° angle; the child names the 130° one

point.hi: Pehla angle phir se 90° ka right angle hai. Jo angle 90° se zyada khula ho par 180° se kam ho, yaani abhi seedhi line na bana ho, use obtuse angle, adhik kon, kehte hain. Doosra angle 130° ka hai.
point.en: The first angle is again the 90° right angle. An angle that opens more than 90° but is less than 180°, so it has not yet become a straight line, is called an obtuse angle. The second angle is 130°.

prompt.hi: Aur yeh 130° wala angle kis type ka hai: acute ya obtuse?
prompt.en: And what type is the 130° angle on the board: acute or obtuse?

why.hi: 130° 90° se zyada aur 180° se kam hai
why.en: 130° is more than 90° and less than 180°

simpler.hi: 90° page ka kona hai, aur 180° ek seedhi line. 130° in dono ke beech aata hai, toh beech wale angle ka naam yaad karo.
simpler.en: 90° is a page corner and 180° is a straight line. 130° sits between the two, so recall the name for an angle in between.

explain.convey: the type depends only on how far the arms are opened, not on how the angle sits on the page: the same square turned tilted keeps every corner at 90° → still right angles

point.hi: Board par do square hain. Pehla seedha rakha hai, uska har kona right angle hai. Doosra wahi square hai, bas tirchha ghuma diya. Square ko ghumaane se uske kone ka khulaav nahi badalta.
point.en: There are two squares on the board. The first sits straight, and each of its corners is a right angle. The second is the same square, just turned tilted. Turning the square does not change how far its corners are opened.

prompt.hi: Toh tirchhe square ka kona kis type ka angle hai: right ya acute?
prompt.en: So what type of angle is the corner of the tilted square: right or acute?

why.hi: tirchha square wahi seedha square hai, toh uske kone ab bhi 90° hain
why.en: the tilted square is the same as the straight one, so its corners are still 90°

simpler.hi: Square ko ghumaao toh bhi uska kona utna hi khula rehta hai. Seedhe square ka kona jis type ka tha, tirchhe ka bhi wahi hai.
simpler.en: Turning a square does not open or close its corners. The tilted square's corner is the same type as the straight square's corner.

problem.hi: Teen angles hain: 25°, 90° aur 145°. Har angle ka type batao: acute, right ya obtuse.
problem.en: There are three angles: 25°, 90° and 145°. Name the type of each: acute, right or obtuse.

simpler.hi: Har angle ko 90° se milao: 90° se kam, 90° ke barabar, ya 90° se zyada.
simpler.en: Compare each angle with 90°: less than 90°, equal to 90°, or more than 90°.

givens.hi: angles 25°, 90° aur 145° hain, aur har ek ko 90° se milaana hai
givens.en: the angles are 25°, 90° and 145°, and each is compared with 90°

find.en: the type of each of the three angles

why.hi: 25° toh 90° se kam hai
why.en: 25° is less than 90°

simpler.hi: 25° ko 90° se milao. 25° chhota hai, page ke kone se kam khula, isliye woh acute hai.
simpler.en: Compare 25° with 90°. 25° is smaller, it opens less than a page corner, so it is acute.

why.hi: yeh theek 90° hai, na kam na zyada
why.en: it is exactly 90°, neither less nor more

simpler.hi: Yeh angle theek 90° ka hai, bilkul page ke kone jaisa. Theek 90° wala angle right angle kehlaata hai.
simpler.en: This angle is exactly 90°, just like a page corner. An angle of exactly 90° is called a right angle.

prompt.hi: Ab 145° ko dekho. Yeh kis type ka hai: acute, right ya obtuse?
prompt.en: Now look at 145°. What type is it: acute, right or obtuse?

simpler.hi: 145° page ke kone 90° se zyada khula hai, par abhi seedhi line nahi bana. Is beech wale angle ka naam yaad karo.
simpler.en: 145° opens more than the 90° page corner but has not yet become a straight line. Recall the name for this in-between angle.

why.hi: 25° aur 90° ke baad bacha 145°, jo 90° se zyada aur 180° se kam hai
why.en: after 25° and 90° comes 145°, which is more than 90° and less than 180°

answer.hi: 25° acute hai, 90° right angle hai aur 145° obtuse hai
answer.en: 25° is acute, 90° is a right angle and 145° is obtuse

why.hi: type sirf naap se tay hota hai: 90° se kam acute, theek 90° right, aur 90° se 180° ke beech obtuse
why.en: the type depends only on the measure: under 90° is acute, exactly 90° is right, between 90° and 180° is obtuse

prompt.hi: Ek square kitaab table par seedhi rakhi thi, ab use tirchhi rakh diya. Kitaab ke kone ka angle kitne degree ka hai?
prompt.en: A square book lay straight on the table, and now it lies tilted. How many degrees is the angle at the book's corner?

why.hi: square kitaab ka har kona 90° hai, aur seedhi ho ya tirchhi, kona utna hi khula rehta hai
why.en: every corner of a square book is 90°, and lying straight or tilted it stays open just as much

simpler.hi: Square ka har kona page ke kone jaisa hota hai. Kitaab tirchhi rakhne se kona nahi badalta, toh page ke kone ke degree yaad karo.
simpler.en: Every corner of a square is like a page corner. Tilting the book does not change the corner, so recall how many degrees a page corner is.

prompt.hi: Ludo board table par seedha rakha tha. Ab use ghumakar tirchha kar diya. Ab board ke kone ka angle kis type ka hai: acute, right ya obtuse?
prompt.en: A ludo board lay straight on the table. Now it has been turned so it sits tilted. What type is the angle at the board's corner now: acute, right or obtuse?

why.hi: ludo board seedha tha tab kona right angle tha, aur tirchha karne se uska khulapan nahi badla
why.en: the ludo board's corner was a right angle lying straight, and turning it tilted did not change its opening

simpler.hi: Board ghumaane se uske kone ka khulaav nahi badalta. Seedhe board ka kona jis type ka tha, ab bhi wahi type hai.
simpler.en: Turning the board does not change how far its corner opens. The corner is still the type it was when the board sat straight.

ladder.why: a cricket bat's 65° turn, the same rule in a real swing
error-spot at the 90° border: 89° and 91° swapped

remediation.move: paper-folded right-angle tester: fold a sheet twice to make a square corner, lay it on corners in many positions (straight, tilted); a corner the tester fits exactly is 90° however it is turned; ask what stayed the same as the page turned

say.hi: Kaagaz ko do baar modkar ek right angle tester banao. Ise seedha ya tirchha, kisi bhi kone par rakho. Tester kone par poora baith jaaye toh kona utna hi khula hai jitna tester, chahe kaise bhi ghooma ho.
say.en: Fold a sheet of paper twice to make a right-angle tester. Put it on any corner, straight or tilted. If the tester fits the corner exactly, the corner opens just as much as the tester, however it is turned.

simpler.hi: Kaagaz do baar modo, tester ban jaata hai. Tester kone par poora baith jaaye toh kona tester jitna hi khula hai, chahe tirchha ho.
simpler.en: Fold paper twice to make a tester. If it fits a corner exactly, the corner opens as much as the tester, even when tilted.

prompt.hi: Deewar par ek photo frame tirchha latka hai. Tester uske kone par poora baith jaata hai. Kona kis type ka angle hai?
prompt.en: A photo frame hangs tilted on the wall. The tester fits its corner exactly. What type of angle is the corner?

why.hi: frame tirchha hai, par tester 90° ka hai aur uske kone par poora baithta hai, toh kona bhi 90° hai
why.en: the frame is tilted, but the 90° tester fits its corner exactly, so the corner is 90° too

simpler.hi: Tester ek square kona hai, aur woh frame ke kone par poora baith gaya. Toh frame ka kona tester ke kone jaisa hi hai.
simpler.en: The tester is a square corner, and it fits the frame's corner exactly. So the frame's corner is the same type as the tester's.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab tak angle 180° se kam khule, jaise 130°. Agle hisse mein arms aur khulenge: pehle bilkul seedhi line tak, yaani 180°, phir usse bhi aage.
bridgeToNext.en: So far the angles opened less than 180°, like 130°. In the next part the arms open further: first all the way to a straight line, 180°, then even beyond it.

simpler.hi: Ab arms aur khulenge, seedhi line tak. Board par ek arm ghoom kar doosri ki ulti disha mein aa gayi hai.
simpler.en: Now the arms open even further, up to a straight line. On the board one arm has turned until it points the opposite way to the other.

hook.convey: turning past obtuse: a U-turn is a half turn (180°, straight angle); a bowler's arm swings more than half a turn (reflex); both are still angles because an angle is an amount of turn

use.hi: Car U-turn leti hai toh woh aadha chakkar ghoomti hai aur ulti disha mein chalne lagti hai. Yeh ghumaav 180° ka hai, aur yeh bhi ek angle hai.
use.en: When a car takes a U-turn it turns half a turn and starts going the opposite way. That turn is 180°, and it is an angle too.

use.hi: Bowler gend daalte waqt arm ko peeche se upar aur phir aage tak ghumata hai. Yeh ghumaav aadhe chakkar se bhi zyada hota hai, yaani 180° se bada angle.
use.en: When a bowler bowls, the arm swings from behind, up over the top and on to the front. That swing is more than half a turn, an angle bigger than 180°.

explain.convey: keep opening past obtuse until the second arm points exactly opposite the first → the arms look like one straight line, but the turn did not vanish: half a turn, 180° = straight angle (rjukon); the child transfers to a book opened flat

point.hi: Doosri arm ghoomte-ghoomte pehli arm ki bilkul ulti disha mein pahunch gayi. Ab dono arms ek seedhi line jaisi dikhti hain, par ghumaav gaayab nahi hua. Yeh aadha chakkar hai, 180°, aur ise straight angle, rjukon, kehte hain.
point.en: The second arm has turned until it points in exactly the opposite direction to the first. Now the two arms look like one straight line, but the turn has not vanished. It is half a turn, 180°, and it is called a straight angle.

prompt.hi: Kitaab table par poori khuli hai, dono cover board ki arms jaise ulti disha mein. Covers ke beech kaunsa angle hai: obtuse ya straight angle?
prompt.en: A book lies fully open on the table, its two covers pointing opposite ways like the arms on the board. What angle is between the covers: obtuse or straight angle?

why.hi: dono cover ulti disha mein hain, yaani aadha chakkar, 180°, jo obtuse se zyada hai
why.en: the covers point opposite ways, half a turn, 180°, which is more than obtuse

simpler.hi: Khuli kitaab ke dono cover ulti disha mein hain, bilkul ek seedhi line jaise. Aisa aadha chakkar 180° hota hai, aur iska apna naam hai.
simpler.en: The open book's two covers point opposite ways, like one straight line. That half turn is 180°, and it has its own name.

explain.convey: every angle has an outside too: from one arm to the other the long way round; inside + outside = a full turn, 360°; board: an inside angle of 100°; the child finds the outside one

point.hi: Board par andar wala angle 100° ka hai. Par ek arm se doosri arm tak lambe raaste se, bahar ki taraf ghoomkar bhi pahunch sakte hain. Woh bahar wala angle hai. Andar aur bahar wala angle milkar poora chakkar banate hain, 360°.
point.en: The inside angle on the board is 100°. But you can also get from one arm to the other the long way, turning round the outside. That is the outside angle. The inside and outside angles together make a full turn, 360°.

prompt.hi: Toh is 100° wale angle ka bahar wala angle kitne degree ka hai?
prompt.en: So how many degrees is the outside angle of this 100° angle?

why.hi: andar aur bahar wala angle milkar 360° hain, aur 360° − 100° = 260°
why.en: the inside and outside angles make 360° together, and 360° − 100° = 260°

simpler.hi: Andar aur bahar ke angle milkar poora chakkar, 360°, banate hain. Toh andar ka 100° 360° mein se hatao.
simpler.en: Together, the inside and outside angles make a full turn, 360°. So take the inside 100° away from 360°.

explain.convey: an angle more than 180° and less than 360° = reflex (prativarti kon); board: inside 120° (obtuse), outside 360° − 120° = 240°; the child names the 240° one

point.hi: Is angle ka andar wala hissa 120° hai, yeh obtuse hai. Bahar wala hissa 360° − 120° = 240° hai. Jo angle 180° se zyada aur 360° se kam ho, use reflex angle, prativarti kon, kehte hain.
point.en: The inside part of this angle is 120°; it is obtuse. The outside part is 360° − 120° = 240°. An angle more than 180° and less than 360° is called a reflex angle.

prompt.hi: Toh bahar wala 240° ka angle kis type ka hai: obtuse ya reflex?
prompt.en: So what type is the 240° outside angle: obtuse or reflex?

why.hi: andar 120° hai, toh bahar 240°, jo 180° se zyada aur 360° se kam hai
why.en: the inside is 120°, so the outside is 240°, which is more than 180° and less than 360°

simpler.hi: 240° seedhi line ke 180° se bada hai, par poore chakkar 360° se chhota. Is range wale angle ka naam abhi seekha.
simpler.en: 240° is more than the 180° of a straight line but less than a full 360° turn. You just learned the name for angles in this range.

problem.hi: A, O aur C ek seedhi line par hain, O beech mein. Ray OB aisi hai ki angle AOB = 50°. Angle AOC, angle BOC aur angle AOB ka bahar wala angle nikalo, aur har ek ka type batao.
problem.en: A, O and C lie on one straight line, with O in the middle. Ray OB is such that angle AOB = 50°. Find angle AOC, angle BOC and the outside angle of AOB, and name the type of each.

simpler.hi: Teen angle ek-ek karke nikalenge. Pehla angle AOC hai, jo seedhi line par bana hai.
simpler.en: We find the three angles one at a time. The first is angle AOC, which lies along a straight line.

givens.hi: A, O aur C ek seedhi line par hain, O beech mein, aur angle AOB 50° hai
givens.en: A, O and C are on one straight line with O in the middle, and angle AOB is 50°

find.hi: angle AOC, angle BOC aur AOB ka bahar wala angle, unke type ke saath
find.en: angle AOC, angle BOC and the outside angle of AOB, with their types

steps.result: angle AOC = 180°, yeh straight angle hai

why.hi: OA aur OC ulti disha mein hain, yaani aadha chakkar
why.en: OA and OC point in opposite directions, which is half a turn

simpler.hi: OA aur OC ek hi seedhi line ke do ulte hisse hain. Seedhi line ka angle 180° hota hai, yeh straight angle hai.
simpler.en: OA and OC are the two opposite halves of one straight line. A straight line's angle is 180°, a straight angle.

why.hi: AOB aur BOC milkar seedhi line ka 180° banate hain, aur 130° toh 90° aur 180° ke beech hai
why.en: AOB and BOC together make the straight line's 180°, and 130° lies between 90° and 180°

simpler.hi: Seedhi line ka 180° do hisson mein bata hai. Ek hissa 50° hai, toh baaki hissa 180° − 50° = 130° hai.
simpler.en: The 180° of the straight line is split into two parts. One part is 50°, so the other is 180° − 50° = 130°.

do.hi: AOB ka bahar wala angle nikalo: poore chakkar mein se 50° ghatao
do.en: Find the outside angle of AOB: subtract 50° from a full turn

why.hi: andar aur bahar wala angle milkar poora chakkar, 360°, banate hain
why.en: the inside and outside angles together make a full turn, 360°

simpler.hi: Poora chakkar 360° hai. Andar ka 50° hata do, toh bahar wala 310° bachta hai.
simpler.en: A full turn is 360°. Take away the inside 50° and the outside 310° is left.

prompt.hi: Ab yeh 310° wala angle kis type ka hai: obtuse, straight ya reflex?
prompt.en: Now what type is this 310° angle: obtuse, straight or reflex?

simpler.hi: 310° seedhi line ke 180° se bada hai aur poore chakkar 360° se chhota. Aise angle ka naam yaad karo.
simpler.en: 310° is more than the 180° of a straight line and less than a full 360° turn. Recall the name of such an angle.

why.hi: AOB ka bahar wala 310° hai; angle BOC 180° se kam hai, par yeh 180° aur 360° ke beech hai
why.en: the outside of AOB is 310°; angle BOC is under 180°, but this one lies between 180° and 360°

answer.hi: angle AOC = 180° straight angle hai, angle BOC = 130° obtuse hai, aur AOB ka bahar wala angle 310° reflex hai
answer.en: angle AOC = 180° is a straight angle, angle BOC = 130° is obtuse, and the outside angle of AOB, 310°, is reflex

why.hi: ulti disha ki arms 180° banati hain, andar aur bahar milkar 360° hain, aur 180° se 360° ke beech reflex hai
why.en: opposite arms make 180°, the inside and outside angles add to 360°, and an angle between 180° and 360° is reflex

prompt.hi: 6 baje ghadi ki dono suiyan ulti disha mein hoti hain. Unke beech ka angle kitne degree ka hai?
prompt.en: At 6 o'clock the two hands of a clock point in opposite directions. How many degrees is the angle between them?

why.hi: 6 baje suiyan ulti disha mein hain, aadha chakkar, aur 360° ka aadha 180° hai
why.en: at 6 o'clock the hands point opposite ways, half a turn, and half of 360° is 180°

simpler.hi: 6 baje ek sui upar aur ek neeche hoti hai, dono milkar ek seedhi line banati hain. Seedhi line ka angle yaad karo.
simpler.en: At 6 o'clock one hand points up and one down, making one straight line. Recall the angle of a straight line.

prompt.hi: Ek angle 70° ka hai. Uska bahar wala angle, lambe raaste se, kitne degree ka hai?
prompt.en: An angle is 70°. How many degrees is its outside angle, the long way round?

why.hi: andar aur bahar milkar 360° hain, aur 360° − 70° = 290°
why.en: inside and outside make 360° together, and 360° − 70° = 290°

simpler.hi: Andar plus bahar poora chakkar hota hai. Toh poore chakkar ke degree mein se 70° hatao.
simpler.en: Inside plus outside is a full turn. So take 70° away from a full turn's degrees.

prompt.hi: Ek angle ka andar wala hissa 125° hai aur bahar wala 235°. Bahar wala angle kis type ka hai: obtuse, straight ya reflex?
prompt.en: The inside part of an angle is 125° and the outside part is 235°. What type is the outside angle: obtuse, straight or reflex?

why.hi: andar 125° hai aur bahar 235°, jo 180° se zyada aur 360° se kam hai
why.en: the inside is 125° and the outside 235°, which is more than 180° and less than 360°

simpler.hi: 235° ko seedhi line se milao, jo aadha chakkar hai. Jo angle seedhi line se bada ho par poore chakkar se chhota, uska naam yaad karo.
simpler.en: Compare 235° with a straight line, which is half a turn. Recall the name of an angle bigger than a straight line but smaller than a full turn.

ladder.why: a book opened flat → there is an angle, 180°
3 o'clock the long way round: 360° − 90° = 270°, reflex
a game arrow turning 210° → reflex, not straight

remediation.move: angle-maker opened slowly from acute through right and obtuse to flat; the child names each stop; at flat: did the turn suddenly vanish, or is it half a full turn?

say.hi: Angle-maker ko dheere-dheere kholo: pehle acute, phir right, phir obtuse. Aur kholo toh dono arms ek seedh mein aa jaati hain. Ghumaav gaayab nahi hua, yeh aadha chakkar hai.
say.en: Open the angle-maker slowly: first acute, then right, then obtuse. Open it more and the two arms come into one line. The turn has not vanished; it is half a turn.

simpler.hi: Angle-maker kholte jao: acute, right, obtuse. Arms ek seedh mein aa jaayein, tab bhi ghumaav hai, aadha chakkar.
simpler.en: Keep opening the angle-maker: acute, right, obtuse. When the arms come into one line, there is still a turn, half a turn.

prompt.hi: Pankhe ka blade khidki ki taraf se ghoomkar bilkul ulti disha mein ruka. Blade kitne degree ghooma?
prompt.en: A fan blade turned from pointing at the window to pointing exactly the opposite way. How many degrees did it turn?

why.hi: blade ulti disha tak ghooma, yaani aadha chakkar, aur 360° ka aadha 180° hai
why.en: the blade turned to face the opposite way, half a turn, and half of 360° is 180°

simpler.hi: Blade ulti disha mein ruka, yaani aadha chakkar ghooma. Aadhe chakkar ke degree yaad karo, jo seedhi line ke hote hain.
simpler.en: The blade stopped facing the opposite way, so it turned half a turn. Recall the degrees in half a turn, the same as a straight line.

remediation.move: clock hands with the small and the large angle shaded in different colours; the child shades the outside part and adds the two: small + large = full turn 360°

say.hi: Ghadi mein 3 baje suiyon ke beech chhota angle 90° hai. Ab bahar ka bada hissa doosre rang se bharo. Dono hisse milkar poora chakkar, 360°, banate hain, toh bahar wala 270° hai.
say.en: At 3 o'clock the small angle between the hands is 90°. Now shade the big outside part in another colour. The two parts together make a full turn, 360°, so the outside one is 270°.

simpler.hi: 3 baje chhota angle 90° hai. Dono hisse milkar 360° hain, toh bahar wala 270° hai.
simpler.en: At 3 o'clock the small angle is 90°. The two parts make 360°, so the outside one is 270°.

prompt.hi: Ghadi ki suiyon ke beech chhota angle 80° hai. Lambe raaste wala bada angle kitne degree ka hai?
prompt.en: The small angle between a clock's hands is 80°. How many degrees is the big angle the long way round?

why.hi: chhota angle 80° hai, dono milkar 360°, toh 360° − 80° = 280°
why.en: the small angle is 80°, the two make 360°, so 360° − 80° = 280°

simpler.hi: Chhota aur bada angle milkar poora chakkar banate hain. Toh poore chakkar ke degree mein se 80° ghatao.
simpler.en: The small and big angles together make a full turn. So take 80° away from a full turn's degrees.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab paanchon type pata hain: acute, right, obtuse, straight aur reflex. Agle hisse mein inhe asli cheezon mein dhoondhenge: ghadi ki suiyon mein aur sadkon ke chauraahe par.
bridgeToNext.en: Now you know all five types: acute, right, obtuse, straight and reflex. In the next part we will find them in real things: in clock hands and at road crossings.

simpler.hi: Ab in types ko asli cheezon mein dhoondhenge. Board par ghadi ki suiyon se bane do angle hain.
simpler.en: Now we find these types in real things. On the board there are two angles made by clock hands.

hook.convey: angles live in real things: two roads meeting at a crossing make four corners; branches leaving a tree trunk; the measure decides the type every time

use.hi: Bus chauraahe se guzarti hai toh dekho: wahan do seedhi sadkein milti hain aur chaar kone banati hain. Har kone ka apna angle hai, aur uska naap hi batata hai woh kis type ka hai.
use.en: When a bus goes through a crossing, look: two straight roads meet there and make four corners. Each corner has its own angle, and its measure tells us which type it is.

use.hi: Tree ki har shaakh tane se ek angle banati hai. Koi shaakh tane ke paas sata hua chhota angle banati hai, koi khul kar bada.
use.en: Every branch of a tree makes an angle with the trunk. One branch makes a small angle close to the trunk, another opens out into a big one.

explain.convey: a clock is a full turn of 360° in 12 equal hour-spaces → each space 360 ÷ 12 = 30°; at 3 o'clock the hands are 3 spaces apart = 90°; board: 3 o'clock and 5 o'clock angles; the child finds the 5 o'clock one

point.hi: Ghadi ka poora chakkar 360° hai. Ek ghante ke nishaan se agle nishaan tak 360 ÷ 12 = 30° hota hai. 3 baje ghante wali sui 12 se 3 tak ghoomi hai, toh 3 × 30° = 90°, right angle. Board par 5 baje wala angle bhi bana hai.
point.en: A clock's full turn is 360°. From one hour mark to the next is 360 ÷ 12 = 30°. At 3 o'clock the hour hand has turned from 12 to 3, so 3 × 30° = 90°, a right angle. The 5 o'clock angle is on the board too.

prompt.hi: Board par 5 baje wala chhota angle kitne degree ka hai?
prompt.en: How many degrees is the smaller 5 o'clock angle on the board?

why.hi: 3 baje 90° tha; 5 baje sui 12 se 5 tak paanch ghante ghoomi, aur 5 × 30° = 150°
why.en: at 3 o'clock it was 90°; at 5 o'clock the hand turned five hours from 12, and 5 × 30° = 150°

simpler.hi: Ghadi mein har ghanta 30° ka hai. 5 baje sui 12 se 5 tak paanch ghante ghoomi, toh 30° ko 5 baar jodo.
simpler.en: On a clock each hour is 30°. At 5 o'clock the hand turned five hours from 12 to 5, so add 30° five times.

explain.convey: two straight roads crossing: one road is a straight angle, 180°; the other road splits that 180° into two neighbouring corners → neighbours on one road add to 180°, so they are NOT all equal; board: the straight road and a 60° corner; the child finds the neighbour

point.hi: Board par do seedhi sadkein ek chauraahe par ek-doosre ko kaat-ti hain. Pehli sadak seedhi hai, toh uske ek taraf ka angle 180° hai. Doosri sadak is 180° ko baantkar do bagal wale kone banati hai. Ek kona 60° ka hai, aur bagal wala kona baaki bacha hissa hai. Dono bagal wale kone milkar 180° banate hain.
point.en: On the board two straight roads cross each other at a crossing. The first road is straight, so the angle on one side of it is 180°. The second road splits this 180° into two neighbouring corners. One corner is 60°, and the neighbouring corner is the part that is left. The two neighbouring corners together make 180°.

prompt.hi: Toh 60° wale kone ke bagal wala kona kitne degree ka hai?
prompt.en: So how many degrees is the corner next to the 60° corner?

why.hi: dono kone seedhi sadak ke 180° ko baantte hain, aur 180° − 60° = 120°
why.en: the two corners share the straight road's 180°, and 180° − 60° = 120°

simpler.hi: Seedhi sadak ke ek taraf 180° hai, jo do kono mein bata hai. Ek kona 60° hai, toh 180° mein se 60° ghatao.
simpler.en: One side of a straight road is 180°, shared by two corners. One corner is 60°, so take 60° from 180°.

explain.convey: at a crossing the four corners come in two pairs: opposite corners are equal, neighbours add to 180°; board: a 65° corner and its 115° neighbour; the child types the corner opposite the 115° one (not the one it sees)

point.hi: Chauraahe par chaar kone bante hain. Bagal wale kone milkar 180° banate hain, aur aamne-saamne ke kone barabar hote hain. Board par ek kona 65° ka hai aur uska bagal wala kona 115° ka.
point.en: At a crossing four corners form. Neighbouring corners add up to 180°, and opposite corners are equal. On the board one corner is 65° and its neighbour is 115°.

prompt.hi: 115° wale kone ke theek saamne wala kona kis type ka hai: acute ya obtuse?
prompt.en: What type is the corner directly opposite the 115° corner: acute or obtuse?

why.hi: saamne wala kona 115° ke barabar hai, jo 90° se zyada aur 180° se kam hai
why.en: the opposite corner equals 115°, which is more than 90° and less than 180°

simpler.hi: Aamne-saamne ke kone barabar hote hain, toh saamne wala kona bhi 115° ka hai. Ab dekho 115° page ke kone se kam khula hai ya zyada.
simpler.en: Opposite corners are equal, so the opposite corner is also 115°. Now see if 115° opens less or more than a page corner.

problem.hi: Deewar ki ghadi mein theek 10 baje hain. Ghadi ka poora chakkar 360° hai aur usmein 12 ghante hain. Suiyon ke beech ka chhota angle aur bada angle nikalo, aur dono ka type batao.
problem.en: A wall clock shows exactly 10 o'clock. A clock's full turn is 360°, with 12 hours on it. Find the smaller and the larger angle between the hands, and name the type of each.

simpler.hi: Deewar ki ghadi mein theek 10 baje hain, aur ghadi ka poora chakkar 360° hai. Suiyon ke beech ka chhota angle, bada angle aur dono ke type chahiye.
simpler.en: A wall clock shows exactly 10 o'clock, and the clock's full turn is 360°. We need the smaller angle, the larger angle and the type of each.

givens.hi: minute wali sui 12 par, ghante wali sui 10 par, aur 360° ke chakkar mein 12 ghante
givens.en: the minute hand is on 12, the hour hand on 10, and a 360° turn holds 12 hours

find.hi: chhota aur bada angle, unke type ke saath
find.en: the smaller and the larger angle, with their types

do.hi: Ek ghante ka angle nikalo: 360° ko 12 se bhaag do
do.en: Find one hour's angle: divide 360° by 12

why.hi: poore chakkar mein 12 ghante hain, sab ek jaise
why.en: a full turn holds 12 hours, all alike

simpler.hi: Poora chakkar 360° hai aur ghadi par 12 ghante hain. 360° ko 12 se bhaag do, toh har ghanta 30° ka.
simpler.en: A full turn is 360° and the clock shows 12 hours. Divide 360° by 12 and each hour is 30°.

do.hi: 10 se 12 tak chhote raaste ke ghante lo
do.en: Take the hours from 10 to 12 the short way

why.hi: ghante wali sui 10 par aur minute wali 12 par hai, beech mein do ghante
why.en: the hour hand is on 10 and the minute hand on 12, two hours apart

simpler.hi: Chhote raaste se 10 se 12 tak do ghante hain. Har ghanta 30° ka, toh 2 × 30° = 60°.
simpler.en: The short way from 10 to 12 is two hours. Each hour is 30°, so 2 × 30° = 60°.

why.hi: 60° toh 90° se kam hai, isliye chhota angle acute hai
why.en: 60° is less than 90°, so the smaller angle is acute

simpler.hi: 60° page ke kone se kam khula hai. Kone se kam khula angle acute hota hai.
simpler.en: 60° opens less than a page corner. An angle that opens less than a corner is acute.

prompt.hi: Ab lambe raaste wala bada angle nikalo. 360° − 60° kitna hota hai?
prompt.en: Now find the larger angle the long way round. What is 360° − 60°?

simpler.hi: Chhota aur bada angle milkar poora chakkar 360° banate hain. Toh 360° mein se chhota 60° hata do.
simpler.en: Together the small and large angles make a full 360° turn. So take the small 60° away from 360°.

why.hi: 10 baje chhota angle 60° hai, aur dono milkar 360° hain, toh 360° − 60° = 300°
why.en: at 10 o'clock the small angle is 60°, and the two make 360°, so 360° − 60° = 300°

answer.hi: chhota angle 60° acute hai aur bada angle 300° reflex hai
answer.en: the smaller angle is 60°, acute, and the larger angle is 300°, reflex

why.hi: ghadi ka har ghanta 30° hai, dono angle milkar 360° banate hain, aur 180° se bada angle reflex hota hai
why.en: each clock hour is 30°, the smaller and larger angles add to 360°, and the larger one, more than 180°, is reflex

prompt.hi: Do seedhi sadkein ek chauraahe par milti hain. Ek kona 40° ka hai. Uske bagal wala kona, jo ek sadak share karta hai, kitne degree ka hai?
prompt.en: Two straight roads meet at a crossing. One corner is 40°. How many degrees is the corner next to it, sharing one road?

why.hi: dono kone ek seedhi sadak ke 180° ko baantte hain, aur 180° − 40° = 140°
why.en: the two corners share one straight road's 180°, and 180° − 40° = 140°

simpler.hi: Bagal wale do kone sadak ke ek taraf milkar seedhi line banate hain. Seedhi line ke degree mein se 40° ghatao.
simpler.en: The two neighbouring corners on one side of the road together make a straight line. Take 40° away from a straight line's degrees.

prompt.hi: 1 baje suiyon ke beech chhota angle 30° hai. Lambe raaste wala bada angle kitne degree ka hai?
prompt.en: At 1 o'clock the small angle between the hands is 30°. How many degrees is the large angle the long way round?

why.hi: 1 baje chhota angle 30° hai, dono milkar 360°, toh 360° − 30° = 330°
why.en: at 1 o'clock the small angle is 30°, the two make 360°, so 360° − 30° = 330°

simpler.hi: Dono angle milkar poora chakkar banate hain. Poore chakkar ke degree mein se 30° hatao.
simpler.en: Both angles together make a full turn. Take 30° away from a full turn's degrees.

ladder.why: 8 o'clock the short way: 4 gaps × 30° = 120° → obtuse
a crossing with one 70° corner → all four corners and their types

remediation.move: two strips pinned at the crossing: strip 1 fixed as a straight road = 180°; rotate strip 2 → one corner grows while its neighbour shrinks → neighbours on one road always add to 180°

say.hi: Ek lakdi ki dandi ko seedhi sadak maan lo, uska angle 180° hai. Doosri dandi ko beech mein pin karke ghumao: ek kona khulta hai toh bagal wala utna hi band hota hai. Dono milkar hamesha 180° rehte hain.
say.en: Take one stick as a straight road; its angle is 180°. Pin a second stick in the middle and turn it: as one corner opens, the neighbouring one closes by the same amount. Together they always stay 180°.

simpler.hi: Seedhi dandi 180° hai. Beech mein doosri dandi ghumao: ek kona khulta hai toh bagal wala utna hi band hota hai. Dono milkar 180° rehte hain.
simpler.en: A straight stick is 180°. Turn a second stick in the middle: as one corner opens, the other closes as much. Together they stay 180°.

prompt.hi: Do seedhi sadkein milti hain. Ek kona 75° ka hai. Uske bagal wala kona kitne degree ka hai?
prompt.en: Two straight roads meet. One corner is 75°. How many degrees is the corner next to it?

why.hi: dono kone ek seedhi sadak ke 180° ko baantte hain, aur 180° − 75° = 105°
why.en: the two corners share one straight road's 180°, and 180° − 75° = 105°

simpler.hi: Bagal wale kone milkar ek seedhi line banate hain. Seedhi line ke degree mein se 75° ghatao.
simpler.en: Neighbouring corners together make a straight line. Take 75° away from a straight line's degrees.

remediation.move: clock hands with both angles shaded in two colours: small + large = full turn 360°; large = 360° − small

say.hi: 3 baje ghadi mein chhota angle 90° hai. Bahar ka bada hissa doosre rang se bharo. Dono hisse milkar 360° banate hain, toh bada angle 270° hai, reflex.
say.en: At 3 o'clock the small angle is 90°. Shade the big outside part in another colour. The two parts together make 360°, so the large angle is 270°, reflex.

simpler.hi: 3 baje chhota angle 90° hai. Dono hisse milkar 360° hain, toh bada angle 270° hai, reflex.
simpler.en: At 3 o'clock the small angle is 90°. The two parts make 360°, so the large angle is 270°, reflex.

prompt.hi: 5 baje chhota angle 150° hai. Lambe raaste wala bada angle kitne degree ka hai?
prompt.en: At 5 o'clock the small angle is 150°. How many degrees is the large angle the long way round?

why.hi: 5 baje chhota angle 150° hai, dono milkar 360°, toh 360° − 150° = 210°
why.en: at 5 o'clock the small angle is 150°, the two make 360°, so 360° − 150° = 210°

simpler.hi: Chhota aur bada angle milkar poora chakkar banate hain. Poore chakkar ke degree mein se 150° ghatao.
simpler.en: The small and large angles together make a full turn. Take 150° away from a full turn's degrees.
